widgets_values:
## Encode Video and Audio

Encodes the clips and audio coming out of the editor into the latents the sampler works on. Video and audio go through their own VAEs.

### temporal_size

How many frames are encoded at a time. It is set high here because encoding fewer, larger batches is faster when you have the memory for it.

**Lower it if your system struggles.** It is the first value to reduce when encoding runs out of memory, and it changes nothing about the result, only how the work is divided. `temporal_overlap` is how many frames each batch shares with the next.

`tile_size` and `overlap` do the same thing spatially.

### Watch your context frames

⚠️ Pre-context and post-context frames are only useful if there is something under them.

If you select context over an empty stretch of timeline, the emptiness is encoded along with everything else: **black video and silent audio**. The model has no way to know that region was meant to be nothing, so it reads as real content and pulls the generation hard toward opening black and quiet.

Before rendering, check that the context range actually sits over footage.

widgets_values:
## Sonder Save Video

Encodes the render into a real project asset, and optionally places it back on the timeline.

### mode

- **Take** saves the clip *and* drops it onto the timeline as a new lane, ready to review, compare, or drive the next pass.
- **Video** saves a normal file into the project's media folder and leaves the timeline alone.

### place_audio_on_timeline

Whether the generated audio is placed alongside the take.

Turn it **off** once a section's audio is settled. Later passes over that same section will otherwise stack duplicate copies of the same audio on the timeline.

### mark_queue_complete

- **false** holds the queue on the current section, which is what you want while iterating. Render the same range as many times as you like.
- **true** advances to the next queued section after the render.

### save_preset

- **Editing Master MP4** for intermediate generations. High-fidelity 4:4:4, built for round trips back through the editor, at the cost of a file your browser may not preview.
- **High Quality MP4** for the final clip, exported from inside the editor.

The split matters because intermediate clips are re-encoded every time they pass through another stage. A delivery codec gives up a little on each round trip, and across a first pass, a detail pass, and an upscale pass that adds up.

### color_drift_correction

Leave this on. This helps cushion VAE color drift.

widgets_values:
## Generation Settings

Three controls decide what gets generated and how. All of them are set here or in the editor, never by rewiring the graph.

## Model - Sonder Selector

Choose one of three generation modes. A Sonder Cluster switches the model and its conditioning together as one branch, so the paths you did not pick are never evaluated.

**`fl2va`** is the first/last-frame model.

With no guides on the timeline it behaves as plain **t2va**: prompt in, video and audio out. Place image guides on the timeline and the editor injects them at their frames automatically. There is no separate text-to-video workflow to load and no image-to-video branch to wire. Whether guides exist on the timeline *is* the switch.

**`ref2va`** is the reference model.

Stage References in the editor and each one enters at the section of the timeline you assigned it to. H3's reference node accepts images, videos, the audio carried by those videos, and standalone audio; the Sonder Reference Selector and the Image and Audio Bridges fill those slots from the timeline. A Reference is absent before its span and present during it, without touching the graph.

**`fl2va model with ref2va conditioning`** is a deliberate mismatch, and the subjective one.

This branch feeds the reference model's conditioning into the fl2va model. The rough consensus is that fl2va has the better texture quality and sound, so this trades **weaker reference adherence for a different and arguably nicer finish and audio**.

## Sonder Masks Bridge

Splits the generation window into an independent video mask and audio mask, each switchable between **Edit** and **Freeze**.

Editing one channel while freezing the other means the frozen channel *drives* the generation instead of being regenerated. Freeze the audio and it stays fixed while new video is generated against it. Freeze the video and it drives new audio.

This is also how clips chain into long-form work. Set **precontext frames** in the editor and those frames are frozen, so each new section is generated against the tail of the one before it rather than starting from nothing.


## Sampler/Scheduler - Sonder Selector

Three sampling setups, one low res pass, a detail pass and the final upscale pass. Their actual values are below the selector in case you prefer another combination.

- **First Pass.** Full generation of brand new content.
- **Detail Pass.** Adds high frequency detail to a clip that already exists.
- **Upscale Pass.** A subtle denoise as a final pass, adding a little detail without disturbing what is already there.

### The flow used for the showcase film

Three passes, each at a different resolution, with the sampler setup matched to the job.

1. **540p, First Pass.** Establish the composition and the audio of each clip cheaply. Nothing here is final; the point is to settle what happens and what it sounds like.
2. **1344x768, Detail Pass, audio frozen.** Switch the scene resolution to H3's intended canvas and re-run. The audio is frozen, so it drives the new video instead of being regenerated, and the composition established in step 1 is preserved while detail is added.
3. **1080p, Upscale Pass.** A final, gentler pass above the native canvas. Less aggressive and less resource intensive than the detail pass, for a high resolution finish that does not fight the result you already approved.

Context frames are set on every generation throughout, to carry continuity between clips.

💡 Working small first is the cheap part of this. Composition and audio are what you iterate on, and they are settled at the resolution that costs the least to be wrong at. Generating audio at 50 steps with no turbo LoRA, at a custom resolution of 64x64, gave good audio results when the normal approach was struggling. ⚠️ Treat it as an audio-only trick. The video from that pass is rapid multicolor flashing, playing live in the sampling preview as well as in the saved file, which is a photosensitive-epilepsy risk.

### SeedGenerator
One seed for the whole graph. Its seed output drives both the noise and the Sampler/Scheduler. Be sure to use different seeds for more varied results.


### ModelSamplingMiniMaxH3

Sets H3's two flow shifts.

shift_video is the sampler's actual schedule. Raising it holds sigmas high for longer, so more of the sampling budget goes to composition and motion and less to fine texture.

shift_audio is not a second schedule. The audio rides the same one, and this value decides how far ahead of the picture the audio is denoised. A low value resolves the audio early and fits the video around it; a higher value keeps audio nearer the video's own noise level so the two settle together.

ComfyUI's defaults are 12 / 3. This workflow runs 12 / 6

## Other controls

- **Power Lora Loader**: Setup optional LoRAs of your preference.

## Model Links

**vae**

- [minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors)
- [minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors)

Place both inside a `H3` subfolder. The workflow references them as `H3\<filename>`.

**vae_approx**

- [taeh3.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/MiniMax-H3-TAE/resolve/main/vae_approx/taeh3.safetensors)

A tiny autoencoder used by the **Model Preview Override** node to decode a real video preview while sampling, instead of ComfyUI's usual blurry latent preview. It plays no part in the final output. Goes flat in `vae_approx/`, not in a subfolder. Apache-2.0, by [Kijai](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/MiniMax-H3-TAE).

**diffusion_models**

- [minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors)
- [minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors)

Both are needed. The `fl2va` mode loads the first, the `ref2va` mode the second.

**text_encoders**

- [qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot.safetensors)

This is the one the workflow loads, at roughly 27 GB. [qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors) is a lighter alternative at roughly 16 GB, on hardware with NVFP4 support. Point the CLIPLoader at whichever you install.

**loras**

Place these inside a `H3` subfolder. The workflow references them as `H3\<filename>`, so a flat `loras/` folder will not resolve.

*Speed / sampling*

- [minimax_h3_fl2v_lightx2v_turbo_8step_v1.0_resized_avg_rank_24_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/MiniMax-H3_comfy/resolve/main/loras/minimax_h3_fl2v_lightx2v_turbo_8step_v1.0_resized_avg_rank_24_bf16.safetensors) — first/last-frame turbo distillation, used for the FL2V path.
- [minimax_h3_ref2v_lightx2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_resized_avg_rank_20_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/MiniMax-H3_comfy/resolve/main/loras/minimax_h3_ref2v_lightx2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_resized_avg_rank_20_bf16.safetensors) — reference-to-video turbo distillation, used for the Ref2V path.

Both are Kijai's rank-resized ComfyUI conversions of the originals by [lightx2v / ModelTC](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo) (Apache-2.0). The full-size upstream files work too, but they are several times larger.

*Style*

- [h3-realism-people-t2v-i2v-r2v.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/fal/MiniMax-H3-Realism-People-LoRA/resolve/main/h3-realism-people-t2v-i2v-r2v.safetensors) — photoreal people, by [fal](https://huggingface.co/fal/MiniMax-H3-Realism-People-LoRA). Trigger word **`r34l1sm`**. Intended strength `1.0`; drop to `0.6`–`0.8` for a lighter touch. Works across T2V, I2V and Ref2V.
- [CinematicMH3-V01.safetensors](https://civitai.com/models/2849726?modelVersionId=3217898) — *Cinematic Style LoRA for MiniMax H3* by **Astroburner**, on Civitai. Trigger word **`ASTROCINEMAV01K2T`**.

## Custom Nodes Required

Four packs, all installable through **ComfyUI Manager**. Everything else in this graph is native ComfyUI, including all four MiniMax H3 nodes.

### Sonder Editor

**[ComfyUI-Sonder-Editor](https://github.com/SonderSaid/ComfyUI-Sonder-Editor)** · Manager: `sonder-editor`

The timeline video editor this workflow is built around, and the source of every `Sonder` node here: the Editor itself, the Reference Selector and Bridges, the Guides Bridges, the Masks Bridge, the Selectors, the Cluster, Save Video, and the Metadata Collector.

**Requires Sonder Editor 0.4.0 or newer.** Use this version for the current Reference features and workflow guidance.

### RES4LYF

**[ClownsharkBatwing/RES4LYF](https://github.com/ClownsharkBatwing/RES4LYF)**

Provides the **beta57** scheduler used for the upscale pass and the **SeedGenerator**. The selected **er_sde** sampler and **sgm_uniform** scheduler are native ComfyUI.

### rgthree-comfy

**[rgthree/rgthree-comfy](https://github.com/rgthree/rgthree-comfy)**

Provides the **Power Lora Loader**, which holds the optional style LoRAs in one node instead of a chain of loaders.

⚠️ If you have issues with this node rendering, turn off Nodes 2.0 or just remove this one and replace with your standard lora loader.

### ComfyUI-KJNodes

**[kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes)**

Provides the **Set** and **Get** nodes that carry values across the graph without long wires. There are around a hundred of them here, so without this pack the workflow opens as a field of broken links rather than a graph with a few missing nodes.


**Model Preview Override** replaces ComfyUI's default latent preview with a real decoded video preview while sampling, using the `taeh3` tiny VAE. It earns its place by letting you abandon bad runs early. The composition is readable long before the last step, so you can cancel a generation that clearly is not working and start the next one, instead of sitting through several minutes of sampling to confirm what you already knew at 20%.

### Sonder Editor

**[ComfyUI-Sonder-Editor](https://github.com/SonderSaid/ComfyUI-Sonder-Editor)** · Manager: `sonder-editor`

The timeline video editor this workflow is built around, and the source of every `Sonder` node here: the Editor itself, the Reference Selector and Bridges, the Guides Bridges, the Masks Bridge, the Selectors, the Cluster, Save Video, and the Metadata Collector.

**Requires Sonder Editor 0.4.0 or newer.** Use this version for the current Reference features and workflow guidance.

### RES4LYF

**[ClownsharkBatwing/RES4LYF](https://github.com/ClownsharkBatwing/RES4LYF)**

Provides the **beta57** scheduler used for the upscale pass and the **SeedGenerator**. The selected **er_sde** sampler and **sgm_uniform** scheduler are native ComfyUI.

### rgthree-comfy

**[rgthree/rgthree-comfy](https://github.com/rgthree/rgthree-comfy)**

Provides the **Power Lora Loader**, which holds the optional style LoRAs in one node instead of a chain of loaders.

⚠️ If you have issues with this node rendering, turn off Nodes 2.0 or just remove this one and replace with your standard lora loader.

### ComfyUI-KJNodes

**[kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes)**

Provides the **Set** and **Get** nodes that carry values across the graph without long wires. There are around a hundred of them here, so without this pack the workflow opens as a field of broken links rather than a graph with a few missing nodes.


**Model Preview Override** replaces ComfyUI's default latent preview with a real decoded video preview while sampling, using the `taeh3` tiny VAE. It earns its place by letting you abandon bad runs early. The composition is readable long before the last step, so you can cancel a generation that clearly is not working and start the next one, instead of sitting through several minutes of sampling to confirm what you already knew at 20%.

## Conditioning: Reference to Video

Already wired. Three **Sonder Reference Selector** and Bridge pairs feed the MiniMax H3 reference node, one per media type. You do not connect anything here; you choose which timeline lanes each Selector reads.

| Bridge | Feeds | Capacity |
|---|---|---|
| Reference Image Bridge | `ref_image_0` to `ref_image_8` | 9 pictures |
| Reference Image Bridge | `ref_video_0` to `ref_video_2` | 3 videos |
| Reference Audio Bridge | `ref_audio_0` to `ref_audio_2` | 3 standalone audio |

Videos go through the **Image** Bridge, not a separate video one. The Audio Bridge is only for standalone audio References.

### Empty slots do not influence the generation, so you can leave them always wired.

Every Bridge here has **`unused_slots` set to `nothing`**:

- **`placeholder`**, the default, emits a black image at scene size or a one second silent track. Nodes with *required* inputs need that.
- **`nothing`** emits no value at all, and H3's reference inputs are optional, so the model skips the slot entirely.

If these were left on `placeholder`, every unfilled slot would hand H3 a black frame or a second of silence **as a real reference**. Leave them on `nothing`.

### Setting this up for a new scene

The scenes in this project are already configured. Lanes 0,1,2,3 for Pictures. Lanes 4,5,6 for Audio, and no lanes for Video because video references were not used.

For a new one:

1. In each Selector, choose which Reference lane or lanes make up its set. The Selector panel edits this list; `reference_lanes` is comma separated and zero based.
2. Wire that Selector's `reference_set` into the Image Bridge or the Audio Bridge, depending on the media type of those lanes.

Lanes you name that do not exist are skipped. They do not quietly fall back to lane zero.

### Keep lane order consistent across scenes

⚠️ A Bridge decodes **homogeneous** lanes: every lane in one set has to be the same media type.

So if Reference lane 1 holds pictures in one scene and audio in another, rendering the second scene throws an error, because an audio lane has arrived at a node whose outputs are images.

Decide an order per media type once, and keep it across every scene in the project. Pictures always on the picture lanes, audio always on the audio lanes. Do that and you can jump between scenes and render each one without touching the graph.

nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward.

MiniMax describes H3 as reaching 2K and roughly 15 seconds. The open weights this workflow runs on work at H3's native canvas of a **768px short edge, up to 1344x768, at 24fps**.

## About this workflow

This workflow was submitted to the Comfy H3 Sync Challenge alongside the [entry video](https://youtu.be/n-NdAQk7I8A). The video was produced entirely with this workflow, without external post-production, color correction, or audio correction.

The graph is staged by the **Sonder Editor**. You arrange clips, image guides, References, and prompts on the timeline, mark the range you want, and the editor supplies the graph with the prompt, dimensions, length, and every conditioning input for exactly that range.

**Nothing in the graph needs rewiring, muting, or bypassing to change what you generate.** Every choice is made in the editor or in a Sonder Selector.

### What it does

- **Three generation modes.** `fl2va`, `ref2va`, and a hybrid that runs reference conditioning through the fl2va model.
- **Text, keyframe, and reference driven generation from one graph.** Guides and References on the timeline decide which, not rewiring.
- **References that respect time.** A Reference enters at the section you assigned it to, and is absent everywhere else.
- **Independent video and audio masks.** Regenerate one channel while the other drives it.
- **Long-form chaining.** Frozen precontext frames carry each section into the next.
- **Three sampling passes.** One for new content, one for detail, one for a final upscale.
- **Native synchronized audio throughout.** Speech, effects, and music are generated with their picture, never stitched on afterward.

> Each of these is covered in depth in the **Generation Settings** note.

## Set these two in the editor first ⚠️

Both are one-time per project, and both fail quietly if you skip them.

**1. Model template -> MiniMax H3.** In the toolbar above the timeline. This is what makes the editor calculate resolution and length on H3's grid: fixed 24fps, dimensions in multiples of 32, and lengths on the 17n+5 frame grid. Without it the editor has no model constraints to snap to and the numbers it hands the graph will not be valid H3 sizes.

**2. Channels template -> MiniMax H3 (full reference).** In the toolbar or in the editor settings. This is what lets References attach themselves to prompts, by giving the prompt the six reference sections H3 expects for subjects, pictures, video and audio.

⚠️ Pick the right one: the channels list also contains a preset called plain **MiniMax H3**, which is the three-field text and keyframe format. It is a valid choice for `fl2va` work, but References will not attach to it. The one with **(full reference)** in the name is the one this workflow is built around.

> 📖 **[Reference guide](https://github.com/SonderSaid/ComfyUI-Sonder-Editor/blob/main/docs/references.md)**: the full walkthrough of staging References, assigning spans, and attaching them to prompt sections.

### Learn more about Sonder Editor

This workflow is deliberately narrow. It covers MiniMax H3 and the Reference system, and leaves the rest of the editor out.

The **[Sonder LTX 2.3 Playground](https://github.com/SonderSaid/ComfyUI-Sonder-Editor/blob/main/example_workflows/sonder_ltx_2_3_playground.json)** is the wide version, and the place those features are explained properly. Every node in it carries its own note, and its notes explain four example scenes:

- **Interrogation, T2V Prompt Relay.** One global prompt plus timed local prompts driving motion, expression, and scene changes with no guides or drivers at all.
- **Interrogation, Upscale / Detail.** The same clip refined through separate 720p and 1080p passes, with the denoise values, batch sizes, and context-frame counts each pass actually used, and how to retake a bad seam without redoing the scene.
- **Pretty People, I2V.** Image guides placed at chosen frames, which is a more flexible form of first-frame / last-frame work.
- **Dance, T2V IC-LoRA Driver.** A pose clip driving generation without being rendered itself, and how to switch the whole driver branch off for sections that have no driver.

It also covers the parts this workflow does not touch: batching a long timeline through the render queue, comparing takes in the gallery, and recording what produced each result with the Metadata Collector.

Repository and written guides: **[ComfyUI-Sonder-Editor](https://github.com/SonderSaid/ComfyUI-Sonder-Editor#documentation)**.
